nodes.name: ERP Account Number (Filter)
nodes.notes: TYPE THE ERP ACCOUNT NUMBER HERE before running, e.g. 10981, to draft for that one customer. Leave it blank to draft for every account Printing Letter_Invoices returns. This is the only field you need to touch for a normal single-account run.

nodes.name: Printing Letter_Invoices
nodes.notes: Returns one item per account, carrying the letter content and the customer number. The email address and the statement are both sourced from Business Central further down.

nodes.name: Normalize Account Fields
nodes.notes: Fallback chains cover both Business Central shapes: OData page fields (No, Name, Company_Name, Integration_Customer_No) and API v2.0 fields (number, displayName, companyName). Trim to the single real field name once the Printing Letter_Invoices export is available. accountNumber must end up as the customer number (e.g. 10981) — it is the key for both the contact lookup and the statement.

conditions.leftValue: ={{ (() => { const f = ($('ERP Account Number (Filter)').first().json.erpAccountNumber ?? '').toString().trim(); return !f || f === ($json.accountNumber ?? '').toString().trim(); })() }}

nodes.name: Matches ERP Filter?
nodes.notes: Blank filter lets every account through; a filter value keeps only the account whose number matches exactly. If you typed a number and everything lands in the 'Filtered Out' branch, the number does not match what Printing Letter_Invoices emits — check for leading zeros or padding.

nodes.name: Filtered Out — Different Account
nodes.notes: Accounts excluded by the ERP filter. On a single-account run every other account lands here, which is expected. If ALL accounts land here, the ERP number you typed matched nothing.

nodes.name: Require Account Number
nodes.notes: Guard: an empty account number would turn the BC $filter into a match-everything query and would render the wrong account's statement.

nodes.name: Look Up AP Contact (Business Central)
nodes.notes: Queries the Contact List page (5052 / table 5050) published as the OData web service 'ContactList', filtered to the contact whose Integration Customer No. matches this customer — the CT020141 -> 10981 link. Reads BC_TENANT_ID, BC_ENVIRONMENT and BC_COMPANY_NAME from project Variables. If the published web service has a different name, change the last URL segment.

nodes.name: Render Statement PDF (Business Central)
nodes.notes: Calls the Statement Api codeunit (businesscentral/StatementApi.Codeunit.al) as an OData V4 unbound action. BC cannot return a report as PDF over a plain OData query — $format=PDF is not supported on report web services — so the codeunit renders the report scoped to this customer and returns it base64 encoded in the 'value' property. BC_STATEMENT_REPORT_ID must be set to 50042, the custom statement report Engelman's prints. BC_STATEMENT_REQUEST_XML holds the saved request page parameters that make the statement open-items-only; an empty string accepts the report's defaults.

nodes.name: Statement Base64 → PDF File
nodes.notes: Turns the base64 string Business Central returned into a real binary PDF on the item, under the binary property 'statement', which is what the Outlook node attaches.

nodes.name: Create Outlook Draft (Do Not Send)
nodes.notes: Creates an UNSENT draft only. The draft lands in the mailbox that owns the OAuth2 credential, so this credential must be gpress@engelmansbakery.com. There is deliberately no 'send' operation anywhere in this workflow. Compare the attachment setup here against the RT 21 Daily email workflow and match whichever pattern that one uses.

nodes.name: Skipped — No Email on File
nodes.notes: Accounts whose Business Central contact has no usable E-Mail land here instead of silently disappearing. Review this branch after each run — contactMatchCount of 0 means no contact matched the customer number at all.

nodes.name: Statement Not Rendered — Review
nodes.notes: Accounts whose statement could not be rendered land here so one bad account does not abort the whole batch. Two different things arrive here and the item's error message tells them apart: 'no open ledger entries' means the customer owes nothing and arguably should not have been in the letter run at all, while anything else is a genuine Business Central or auth failure that needs investigating. Do not ignore this branch — a failure here means a customer who should have been chased was not.
